decision.summary: What looked like a routine oven report contains a gas smell, so I treated it as an emergency. I sent the tenant safety advice and the gas line number, opened JOB-102 and escalated P1. I also asked the landlord to decide on the oven repair and put that ticket on hold.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: The oven is still faulty with no provider assigned. The tenant has also reported a gas smell, which is now an emergency ticket (JOB-102). Outstanding: gas engineer dispatch, landlord decision on the oven repair, and the oven repair itself.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: The safety email to the tenant has been sent. The P1 escalation to maintenance is done, to get a Gas Safe engineer out. The landlord has been told and asked about the oven repair.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Yes. A human needs to dispatch the gas engineer as a P1, because there is a possible gas leak and no gas contractor is on file for me to assign.

conflicts: The tenant called the smell 'not urgent', but policy treats any gas smell as an emergency, so I followed policy.
assumptions: The landlord request will go through the landlord record, as no landlord address is shown.

args.body: Hi Imogen, thanks for letting us know. A gassy smell needs treating as an emergency, even if it only happens sometimes. Please: don't use the oven or hob, don't use any flames or light switches near it, open the windows, and leave the flat. Then call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24 hours). If you are ever in immediate danger, call 999. We are arranging an urgent gas safety check and will also look at the oven not heating properly. Please don't use the oven until it has been checked. We will update you today.
